findings.evidence: activate() checks only the status (requireStatus(candidate, ACTIVATABLE)) and then runs retireActive/flush/markActive. It never re-runs validator.validate(candidate.getParameters(), candidate.getCatalogVersion()). Parameters are validated only once, in createDraft (line 48), and the V32 trigger leaves DRAFT/PENDING rows freely editable.
findings.why_it_matters: A draft validated against an older code catalog, or edited after creation, can become the platform ACTIVE version. RubricResolver then fails closed with RUBRIC_VERSION_SCALE_DRIFT (500) for every new template pinned to it. The check belongs before the irreversible step, not after it.
findings.required_action: Before retireActive, re-validate the candidate parameters against the current catalog (validator.validate(...)), so activation is rejected with 400 instead of producing a broken ACTIVE version. This can land with the Phase 9 write API, which is the first production caller.

findings.evidence: Phase step 4 says RubricResolver resolves by examDefinitionPublicId or ACTIVE (practice). The implemented entry points are resolve(UUID versionPublicId, String taskType) and resolveActive(String taskType). Nothing looks up the pinned rubric_version_public_id from an exam definition, although the Javadoc (lines 28-30) says workers read the version pinned on the exam definition of the attempt.
findings.why_it_matters: Phase 3 relies on the mapping from an exam definition to its pin. Leaving it implicit risks a caller resolving ACTIVE instead of the pin.
findings.required_action: Add the examDefinitionPublicId entry point when Phase 3 wires the worker. Use the public assessment ExamDefinitionService / ExamDefinitionResponse.rubricVersionPublicId and define a fallback rule for a legacy null pin. Otherwise, record the deferral in the phase file.

findings.evidence: createDraft computes versionNo = findMaxVersionNo() + 1, so two concurrent drafts collide on uq_scoring_rubric_versions_version_no. With two concurrent activations, the second blocks on retireActive, retires 0 rows, then saveAndFlush hits ux_scoring_rubric_versions_single_active. Both cases surface as a raw DataIntegrityViolationException.
findings.why_it_matters: The data stays correct because the DB constraints catch the race, but the caller gets a 500 instead of a 409 conflict code.
findings.required_action: When Phase 9 exposes the write API, translate these constraint violations into RubricVersionException(CONFLICT, ...) with codes in RubricConstants.

findings.evidence: The ACTIVE -> RETIRED branch excludes retired_at from the row comparison, so an UPDATE that sets status = 'RETIRED' and leaves retired_at NULL passes. Nothing at the DB layer requires activated_at on ACTIVE rows or retired_at on RETIRED rows.
findings.why_it_matters: The service always fills retired_at (retireActive sets retired_at = :now), so this would only add defence in depth.
findings.required_action: Optional, in a later migration (V33+, never by editing an applied V32): CHECK (status <> 'RETIRED' OR retired_at IS NOT NULL), and the same check for ACTIVE/activated_at.

findings.evidence: Testcontainers(disabledWithoutDocker = true): the 12 trigger, index, backfill and flush-order tests were skipped locally and have never run. Reading the SQL and the test statements found no defect: the whole-row to_jsonb comparison is NULL-safe, no trigger on exam_definitions blocks the backfill, and a statement trigger covers TRUNCATE on the audit table. The test for a null pin rejected by the service against a real DB is not written. Nothing writes answer_evaluations.rubric_version_public_id yet (AnswerEvaluation.java:57-59); that is Phase 3 scope.
findings.why_it_matters: The DB layer of the two-layer immutability guarantee has been checked by reading the SQL only, not by running it.
findings.required_action: Run RubricVersionMigrationPostgresTest on the throwaway Postgres (local-dev-runbook) or in CI with Docker before the VPS deploy. Wire the answer_evaluations pin in Phase 3.
